I lived in Philly and watched this whole thing unfold. It was a course set about a year or so before. The Move was what they called themselves most of them were black criminals and muslims. There was some 4-6 families totaling almost 30 people living in a small 3 story row house. Over the course of a year, the number of neighbors called police due to practicing armed drills on the roof, defecating outside the house, housing associated criminals, throwing trash in the back yard, robbing and participating in burglary, etc...

They were vile people and no one liked them. A group of neighborhood residents eventually formed a coalition and together with black council representatives from Philadelphia started picketing outside Mayor Goode's (an incompetent buffoon black guy who spent his tenure giving away money to the blacks in Philly, till Philly almost went bankrupt and every major businesses left) office until he took action. Mayor Goode was aware of the Move group and told police not to incite a riot and buried a lot of bad stories about the Move, very much like Europe is covering up for muslims criminals.

With the neighborhood group mustering support from local council members, Goode was forced to take some action. He sent over firefighters and minimal police officers to clean up around the house and wash it down and remove the urine and feces from around the house and neighborhood. You know when blacks in Philly are complaining about the unsanitary condition, its got to be really really bad.

The Move confronted them sometimes taking shots at them, prompting more police to show up and eventual holding up in the house. For those of you who want to compare this to whats happening in Oregon, no one in Oregon shot at the police first. It got to a point where a good portion of the police force was parked out around the Move house 24/7 for several days.

Because Move was so hostile and heavily armed, and they were shooting at the police, they brought in a helicopter to drop explosives on the roof and breach through the roof. The first attempt failed because Move had fortified the roof with furniture and barricades. So they tried again with a bigger charge. I still remember seeing this. The explosive went off and some of the debris went flying off the roof. It looked like the swat teams were going to drop in and all of a sudden there was smoke.

Out of no where within the span of less than 5 minutes flames started shooting from the roof. Then all hell broke lose. The Move stilled refused to leave the house and began shooting at the police. The police started shooting back until the fire started spreading to the neighbor houses. They pulled back and firefighters couldn't get near because Move kept shooting at the police and firefighters so Mayor Goode made the call to let the fire burn.

It was part of a Philly row house so every house connected to it on the block burned down.

Later, the few remaining Move members eventually left the house and were arrested and I think like 1/3 of them died in the fire.

Its also important to note that, Mayor Goode spent millions of tax payer dollars rebuilding the owners a brand new modern home worth about 4-5 times the value of the homes in 1985 prices. Many blamed his mishandling of the whole Move situation before the conflict and after was his political downfall. He couldn't win the black votes back even after building them $200,000+/house when original prices in the neighborhood was $15-35k. Also it took less than 1-2 years before those $200,000+ homes looked like the original slum houses before the incident.
